subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: Philadelphia Indemnity Ins. Co. (2007) 146 CA4th 565, 579, 52 CR3d 908, 918] b. [3:649] Acts within official capacity: D&O policies typically limit coverage to “wrongful acts” by an officer or director “in the discharge of his duties to the Insured organization in his Insured Capacity, or any matter claimed against him solely by reason of his serving in such Insured Capacity.” [See Olson v. Federal Ins. Co., supra, 219 CA3d at 258-259, 268 CR at 92] • [3:650] Therefore, there is no coverage for acts unrelated to the officer's or director's duties to the corporation. [Olson v. Federal Ins. Co., supra, 219 CA3d at 261, 268 CR at 94—no coverage for claims against director who was also part owner of corporation for acts undertaken as part owner] c. [3:651] Limitation—no coverage where no individual liability: There can be no D&O coverage for acts for which the directors and officers cannot be held liable individually.
